body:
P3-35 SLICE 2 DESIGN (phone; helper-p335, 15 Nov 2026): what must change so that "within minutes" is true ON THE PHONE. Server slice 1 (the link follows the music server's scan, about a minute) is in the PR of branch task/P3-35-new-music-within-minutes. This slice is NOT built: it touches the live events (docs/17, live.py) and the app, which cannot be walked here. No screen: nothing new is drawn.

FACTS (code, main 57941c5):
 a) The 3 to 60 s probe pulls only the person's changes feed (sync_engine.dart:679 `pullChanges`). The files feed, which carries new library songs, is pulled only by `encore.pull()` (encore_sync.dart:83) in a full run (sync_engine.dart:469): every 10 min while open (sync_scheduler.dart:60), on resume after 5 min (:61), on a manual sync, or when the probe says the index is due. After the link: up to 10 min.
 b) A server push does not help as built: `hello`, `library.changed` and `resync` only make a PROBE now (session.dart:540 -> scheduler.liveEvent), and the probe does not pull files. The 6 Nov note "seconds with the push" was wrong on this point.
 c) Artists and albums (the browse index) come from the music server and refresh only when its scan status moved AND `libraryPassGap` has passed since the last full pass: 1 h, 6 h on mobile data (sync_engine.dart:59-60, 632-646). The gap was priced when a pass also downloaded every song (8.6 MB for 6,700, H38); on an Encore server `_runEncore` asks `_libraryPhase(songs: false)`: artists (one request) and album pages only. UNMEASURED: that cost for 6,700 and 200,000 songs; measure first (read-only on VM 108, the lead's bench).
 d) Why the gap exists: every song the KEEPER saves moves the scan status (docs/26 H38). So "the status moved" cannot be the trigger. "The server linked NEW LIBRARY files" can: that is the Host's own music, never a kept song.

PROPOSED (the advisor's call; yours to overrule):
 1. SERVER: `link_library` counts the files it INSERTED with source `library` (the branch `owner is None` in scanner.py; not `MAX(seq)` of `file_log`, which the keeper and meta refreshes also move). `LibraryLinker` gets an `on_new_files(n)` hook; api.py publishes ONE event `files.changed {cursor}` to EVERY connected device (`hub.publish` is per person: add `publish_all`, same full-queue rule as `resync`). Slice 1's floor (60 s and 9x the pass) already rate-limits it. Document it in docs/17 and the live.py module doc.
 2. PHONE: on `files.changed`: `pullFiles()` at once (cursor: cheap, idempotent), then the browse index with the gap waived (`_libraryDue(ignoreGap: true)` is the switch a manual sync already uses), once per event; on mobile data only while the app is open. A phone that was away gets the same at its next full run (unchanged rules).
 3. Do NOT make the probe pull the files feed every 3 s (two requests where one was): that is polling; the push is the source fix and also works for a browser client (ADR-R38). The existing app ignores an event type it does not know (session.dart:540 is a switch with no default), so server first is safe.
 4. TESTS: server: one inserted library file gives exactly one event; a pass that finds nothing new, a kept file, none; every connected person gets it. Phone (fake clock): the event pulls files and runs the index once, a second event after the floor does so again.
 5. WALK on the release-candidate pair: drop an album in the folder with the app open: its songs, then its album and artist, within about 2 minutes.
Size M. Order: after slice 1 is merged. Slice 3 (the Host's "scan now" button and `encore scan`, needs a drawing) is a separate note.
